title: The Ocean's Hidden Bill
paragraphs: The ocean has quietly softened the impact of human emissions. According to the US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, it absorbs about thirty percent of the carbon dioxide released into the atmosphere, slowing the warming that would otherwise occur. This service, however, comes at a chemical price. When carbon dioxide dissolves in seawater it forms carbonic acid, and the average pH of surface waters has fallen by about 0.1 units since the start of the industrial era.

That figure sounds trivial until one recalls that the pH scale is logarithmic: a fall of 0.1 corresponds to an increase of roughly thirty percent in acidity. The term can nonetheless mislead. Seawater remains slightly basic rather than acidic; acidification describes the direction of change, not the destination.

The biological stakes lie mainly in what the extra acid removes. Reactions triggered by the dissolved gas reduce the concentration of carbonate ions, the building blocks that oysters, corals and some pteropods use to construct shells and skeletons. Where carbonate becomes scarce, these organisms must spend more energy to build, and in sufficiently corrosive water existing structures can begin to dissolve. Oyster hatcheries on the Pacific coast of North America have suffered severe losses of larvae, which researchers have linked in part to corrosive water rising from the deep.

The picture is not uniformly bleak. Some seagrasses and algae may grow faster with more carbon dioxide available, and sensitivity varies widely between species and even between populations. Yet organisms rarely face a single stress at a time, and acidification is unfolding alongside warming and falling oxygen levels, which makes the combined outcome harder to forecast than the effect of any single change.

sources.claim: Okyanus atmosfere salınan karbondioksitin yaklaşık yüzde 30'unu emer; CO2 deniz suyunda karbonik asit oluşturur ve karbonat iyonlarını azaltarak istiridye, mercan ve bazı pteropodların (küçük deniz salyangozları) kabuk/iskelet yapımını zorlaştırır; bazı deniz çayırları artan CO2'den yararlanabilir.

Endüstri çağının başından beri yüzey okyanusunun pH'ı yaklaşık 0,1 birim düştü; bu, asitlikte (hidrojen iyonu derişiminde) yaklaşık yüzde 30 artışa karşılık gelir; deniz suyu bazik kalmaya devam eder.
sources.source: NOAA Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory, What is Ocean Acidification?; https://www.pmel.noaa.gov/co2/story/What+is+Ocean+Acidification%3F

sources.claim: ABD'nin Pasifik kuzeybatısındaki istiridye kuluçkahanelerindeki larva kayıpları, derinlerden yükselen aşındırıcı (yüksek CO2'li) suyla ilişkilendirildi.

sources.claim: Okyanuslarda oksijen düzeyleri düşmekte (deoksijenasyon) ve bu süreç ısınma ve asitlenmeyle birlikte deniz yaşamını etkilemektedir.
